title: The Freezer Multisig's stated trigger is Pattern's own non-compliance with Risk Capital or ALM rules
content:
A.6.1.1.6.2.6.1.2.1.2.2.2.4 states when the Freezer should act: signers "should exercise their authority to freeze the Pattern Liquidity Layer in the event that **Pattern is not complying with rules regarding Risk Capital or Asset Liability Management**, or in the event of another emergency."

The primary named trigger is the Agent's own misconduct, not a hack. Read alongside the composition of the multisig — three signers from Operational GovOps Soter Labs, one from Operational Facilitator Redline Facilitation Group, and one from Pattern itself (A.6.1.1.6.2.6.1.2.1.2.2.2.3) — the mechanism is best understood as supervisory rather than defensive. The reviewers hold the brake on the operator, and the operator holds a single key inside the same instrument.

The accountability clause is unusually specific: "Each action executed by the Freezer Multisig, including any function calls and their parameters, must be reported to the Sky community within a reasonable time frame through a post on the Sky Forum." Disclosure is mandatory here ("must"), and extends to parameters — a stricter standard than the discretionary, feasibility-qualified disclosure attached to emergency Root Edits.

The trade-off is discretion. "Should" rather than "must" governs *whether* to freeze, and "another emergency" is undefined at this location, so the decision to act rests on signer judgment while only the reporting of it is compulsory.
description: The emergency brake is aimed at the Agent rather than at external attackers, and every Freezer action including function calls and parameters must be reported publicly on the Sky Forum.
